items.headline: U.S. Equities Trade Mixed Amid Geopolitical Easing and Tech Weakness
items.summary: U.S. stock markets are showing mixed performance in afternoon trading today as optimism from easing U.S.-Iran tensions and a significant drop in oil prices is largely offset by ongoing weakness in the technology sector. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is up, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite are experiencing declines, primarily due to concerns over AI valuations and increased competition from China impacting chip stocks. Investors are also closely watching the Federal Reserve meeting this week for potential policy cues. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Forte Biosciences Leads Gainers
items.summary: Forte Biosciences ($FBRX) surged significantly in today's trading.

items.headline: RTX Corp Rises on Strong Earnings
items.summary: RTX Corp ($RTX) climbed after reporting strong Q2 earnings.

items.headline: SAP Beats Earnings Expectations
items.summary: SAP ($SAP) extended its gains, surging after beating earnings expectations.

items.headline: Nvidia Down Amid Chinese Competition Concerns
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) is trading lower due to increasing concerns about Chinese competition in the semiconductor market.

items.headline: ASML Falls on Chinese Lithography Reports
items.summary: ASML ($ASML) fell sharply following reports that a state-backed Chinese firm has begun producing DUV lithography machines.

items.headline: AMD Slumps Due to Competition
items.summary: AMD ($AMD) experienced a significant drop, also impacted by concerns over increased Chinese competition in the chip sector.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Meeting Set for This Week
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is scheduled to meet on July 28-29. While the Fed is largely expected to keep interest rates unchanged, market participants will be closely scrutinizing any indications of future policy, especially given recent inflationary pressures from Middle East tensions and high tech spending.

items.headline: Oil Prices Plunge as US-Iran Tensions Cool
items.summary: Crude oil prices saw a significant decline today, with Brent crude falling below $90 a barrel and WTI crude dropping nearly 7% to $83.15 a barrel. This sharp retreat is attributed to a pause in strikes between the U.S. and Iran, easing geopolitical tensions and boosting broader market sentiment.

items.headline: Technology Sector Lags Amid Valuation and Competition Concerns
items.summary: The technology sector is a notable laggard today, with major chip stocks like Nvidia and AMD experiencing significant drops. This weakness is driven by renewed concerns over AI valuations and growing competition from state-backed Chinese firms in the DUV lithography machine market.

items.headline: Communication Services and Consumer Defensive Lead Market
items.summary: In contrast to the tech sector, communication services and consumer defensive stocks are among today's top-performing sectors. Airline stocks are also showing strength, benefiting from lower crude oil prices which reduce fuel costs and support margins.

items.headline: June Durable Goods Orders Miss Expectations
items.summary: Headline Durable Goods Orders for June came in at a modest +0.3%, falling short of the consensus estimate of +2%. This suggests that while there is some underlying manufacturing demand, it is seeking equilibrium amidst current economic conditions.

items.headline: Mega-Cap Earnings to Drive Market Volatility This Week
items.summary: This week marks a crescendo in earnings season, with major reports expected from tech giants including Microsoft ($MSFT), Meta Platforms ($META), Apple ($AAPL), and Amazon ($AMZN). Investors will be closely watching these reports for insights into AI infrastructure spending and broader economic trends.
